_comments: THE B2B STAGES. DisplayOrder is the board's left-to-right order; Probability is a DEFAULT copied
onto a deal on entry, not read through — so a deal keeps the number it was judged at when a stage
OrderStatusOnEntry is NULL on the first two. That is an answer, not an omission: Discovery and
Qualification say nothing about the order, and a stage that reset it to Draft on every backward

fields.Name: Discovery
fields.GuidanceMarkdown: **What good looks like:** the economic buyer is named and the current cost of doing nothing is quantified.

fields.Name: Qualification
fields.GuidanceMarkdown: **What good looks like:** budget, authority and a compelling event are all confirmed in writing.

_comments: FROM HERE ON THE ORDER IS QUOTED. A proposal IS a quote, which is why this is the stage where the
answer changes — and why the same value carries through Negotiation and the win rather than
escalating. Escalating to Confirmed is finance's act, not a rep's drag (DN-10).

fields.Name: Proposal
fields.GuidanceMarkdown: **What good looks like:** a priced proposal the champion has seen and can defend internally.

fields.Name: Negotiation
fields.GuidanceMarkdown: **What good looks like:** a mutual action plan with dates, and legal engaged.

_comments: THE WINNING STAGE, and it is called Signed. The status type it points at carries IsWon = 1, which
is the only thing any code reads. Entering it QUOTES the order rather than confirming it: finance
reviews and corrects before the Confirm that books the ledger (S-US5/S-US6).

fields.Name: Signed
fields.GuidanceMarkdown: Agreement executed. Entering this stage quotes the order; finance confirms it, and the Confirm is what books the ledger.

_comments: VOIDING THE ORDER IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW (S-US7). A lost deal's order has to stop being
something finance might act on, and Voided is terminal in orders — which is also what makes the
reopen case in S-US8 warn rather than silently half-succeed.

fields.Name: Lost
fields.GuidanceMarkdown: A loss reason is mandatory — it is the highest-value, most-skipped data in any CRM. Entering this stage VOIDS the order.

_comments: THE D2C STAGES. No proposal step, so only the winning stage speaks about the order — which is the
shape difference that makes shipping both pipelines worth it rather than one.
